prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: [adversarial] Rowspan taller than its rows (language en).
Grid: 3 columns × 4 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Merged cells: "All three steps share on" spans 1 col × 3 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Step" · longest unbreakable word 35px · one-line width 35px
  col 2: header "Owner" · longest unbreakable word 48px · one-line width 48px
  col 3: header "Notes" · longest unbreakable word 76px · one-line width 1797px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 438px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 437px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Show who owns each of three steps and the shared notes that apply to the whole sequence.","reading":"Readers scan the steps and owners row by row, then read the merged Notes cell as context for all three steps. Wrapping in that cell can use the combined height of the three rows; heavier wrapping may make the table taller.","groups":["Step and Owner form paired row-level identifiers; Notes applies to all three rows."],"keep_intact":["Step names and owner names","Unbreakable words in Notes"],"may_wrap":["The shared Notes text can wrap naturally between words."]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r1A: widths [60, 73, 304] · table 438×213px · row heights [36, 59, 59, 59] · column headers wrapped 0/3 · tallest cell 7 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1B: widths [56, 69, 312] · table 438×213px · row heights [36, 59, 59, 59] · column headers wrapped 0/3 · tallest cell 7 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}

log.raw: {"critique":[{"design":"r1A","good":"The Step and Owner columns read as a pair, and the shared note aligns clearly with all three steps. Headers and names stay intact, and the note wraps without splitting words.","problems":"The identifier columns have slightly more space than their short contents need, leaving less room for the long note. The seven-line note ends with a short final line.","cause":"Widths of 60px and 73px give Step and Owner 4px each beyond their respective one-line content requirements; Notes receives 304px."},{"design":"r1B","good":"The tighter Step and Owner columns remain legible and give the note more room. The row boundaries are clear, and the merged cell reads naturally as context for the full sequence. All headers, names, and words remain intact.","problems":"The note still takes seven lines, with a short final line, so the three data rows remain relatively tall.","cause":"Step and Owner are already at their minimum one-line widths of 56px and 69px. Notes has the remaining 312px, which is insufficient to eliminate a line."}],"done":true,"designs":[]}
